name: Drugs for Shock and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

reference.source: KD Tripathi Essentials of Medical Pharmacology 8th Edition and Kaplan Pharmacology (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Vasopressin is second line catecholamine sparing pressor in septic shock
PAH: three pathways (endothelin, nitric oxide, prostacyclin), combine early
Riociguat must never combine with sildenafil (hypotension)
Right ventricle needs systemic pressure, careful preload, pulmonary afterload cut
reference.pathophysiology: Shock is tissue perfusion failure from vessel tone loss, pump failure, volume loss or obstruction, each distorting pressure flow relationships that vasoactive drugs partially restore while cause treatment completes rescue. Pulmonary arterial hypertension instead remodels small pulmonary arteries through endothelin excess, nitric oxide and prostacyclin deficiency, raising right ventricular afterload until the thin ventricle dilates and fails.
additionalDifferentials: Vasodilatory versus cardiogenic shock drug logic
PAH vasoreactive minority versus combination therapy majority
additionalInvestigations: Lactate, capillary refill and urine output perfusion endpoints
Echocardiography for shock classification and right ventricle
Right heart catheterisation confirming precapillary PAH
